newsitem.title: JAPAN: Japan Feb car output falls 1.1 pct due to fire.
newsitem.headline: Japan Feb car output falls 1.1 pct due to fire.

text.p: Vehicle production in Japan slipped in February for the first time in six months because of a fire at a key Toyota Motor parts supplier, an industry body said on Monday.
Domestic vehicle output fell 1.1 percent in February from the same month a year earlier to 933,539 vehicles, the Japan Automobile Manufacturers' Association (JAMA) said.

"If the production loss at Toyota in February was 70,000 cars as Toyota has said, then February's total would have exceeded last year's, so the undertone is still strong. It (the fall) was a passing phenomenon," a JAMA official told Reuters.
In mid-February, Toyota said production losses because of a February 1 fire at a brake parts supplier totalled about 70,000 vehicles.
The fire at Aisin Seiki Co Ltd halted the output of brake parts, forcing Toyota to idle all of its domestic vehicle production lines for nearly four days.
Toyota's actual production loss in February was 67,000 vehicles and Toyota will try to make that up in March, a Toyota spokesman said on Monday.
If there had been no production loss at Toyota, the overall output in February would have reached one million units.
Aisin also supplies parts to Mitsubishi Motors Corp, which saw its output fall by 4,000 cars in February due to the fire. It also plans to recover the loss in March, a Mitsubishi spokesman said.
Toyota's February production fell 13.5 percent from a year earlier to 269,695 units and Mitsubishi's output fell 0.9 percent to 116,519.

"A steep rise in car production in March is expected (because of strong domestic demand ahead of an increase in Japan's consumption tax hike in April), so production for the whole of fiscal 1996/97 is likely to rise about five percent from a year earlier to 10.65 million units and to mark the first gain in six years," the official said.
